quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before turning. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors can adequately show you your surroundings.
Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
Activate your turn signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, in addition to using your mirrors.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip is to:
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on long trips, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Avoid artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even during the day. Reflective clothing is also helpful.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Make your presence known by sounding your horn and/or using lights or signals.

questions.explanation: Communicate your presence to other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed to match the situation and change your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Grabbing at the front brake or jamming down on the rear brake:

options.text: Can cause the brakes to lock.
Is the best way to stop in an emergency.
Is the best way to slow down when the streets are wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the brakes to lock.
questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or pressing the rear brake too hard can lock the brakes. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection on every ride to prevent hearing loss.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are used on many motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make oncoming vehicles look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcycle rider:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you if you crash. They keep you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Go straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: The safest way to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks is to ride straight in your lane. Changing your angle might send you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Move around in your lane based on what you see and what is happening around you.

questions.question: During normal turns:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, both the rider and the motorcycle lean together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider stays more upright to balance it.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar strong material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
Ride on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.explanation: Choose strong footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles that move slower than 25 mph. These include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What must you do to get a motorcycle endorsement?

options.text: Have no traffic violations on your record.

questions.explanation: In Delaware, you must have a valid driver's license before you can apply for a motorcycle endorsement.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it more space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have an accident with another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other cars. The biggest danger is when oncoming cars turn left in front of motorcyclists.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help other drivers see your motorcycle?

options.text: Keep your headlight on high beam.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on high beam.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on, including your running lights if you have them. Use your high beam headlight during the day and at night whenever it is safe and legal.
